answer: Anchor each agent identity to a refundable stake locked in escrow, slashed automatically if the identity misbehaves. A Sybil tide of cheap clones then faces linear cost: every extra identity needs its own locked stake, while an honest agent pays once and recovers it. Like a juniper that only roots where the soil is real, the stake makes bulk forgery unprofitable, because the attacker's capital outlay grows with fleet size while per-identity payout stays flat.
